articles.title: Kushner pushes back on report involving phone, spies, transfer
articles.summary: Jared Kushner is pushing back on a report involving a hacked iPhone, international spies and billion-dollar transfers from foreign governments. An upcoming book by journalist Matthew Cole claims Kushner, who is President Trump's son-in-law, had access to more than $2 billion in "slush money funds" from Middle Eastern leaders in an attempt to influence U.S. foreign policy. An excerpt of the book released Thursday details allegations encompassing Kushner's time as a senior White House adviser during the first Trump administration, which included a lead role in U.S. policy in the Middle East. Kushner had a major hand in negotiating key foreign policy deals that involved Israel, the Gulf states, China and Russia during that period. Kushner and his legal team released fiery statements Thursday night categorically denying all accusations against him. Kushner said , "The allegations made by this author are completely insane and never happened." His attorney called them "false and defamatory" and said they intend to pursue legal action against those responsible, but did not specify whom. The new book, "Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed's Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East," alleges Kushner had access to billions of dollars in undisclosed foreign bank accounts intended to pay for "influence within the U.S. government." An excerpt from the book that was published in "Vanity Fair," but not independently verified by CBS News, says Dutch intelligence agents learned the Russians had hacked Kushner's iPhone in 2017 after flipping a Russian spy and subsequently gained access to Kushner's phone as well. According to the report, "when Kushner used the phone, they could see his screen. Almost as soon as they got inside, the intelligence service began capturing every image of Kushner's screen as he used it." At the time, Kushner served as a senior White House adviser to President Trump, including on Middle Eastern diplomacy. The report alleges Dutch spies witnessed him log into a United Arab Emirates account that had allegedly received hundreds of millions of dollars from a bank in Azerbaijan, and claims the leaders of Saudi Arabia and the UAE put at least $2 billion into multiple bank accounts linked to Kushner, including an account with Israel's Central Bank. According to the book excerpt, the owners and managers of the accounts were often disguised as official government entities or charities, but the funds were actually intended for "off-the-books diplomatic objectives" such as striking a deal to end the Israeli-Palesteinian conflict. The report also claims Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman put roughly $1 billion into at least one account for Kushner, citing a "person with knowledge of the money" saying "its allocation was for Kushner's personal benefit." Kushner forcefully denied the accusations leveled in the "Vanity Fair" excerpt, writing in part, "The allegations made by this author are completely insane and never happened." "We denied every claim on the record, yet the author provided not a single shred of verifiable evidence to substantiate them," he said. "No bank statements, wire transfer records, account numbers, transaction dates, or other verifiable details were provided to support these extraordinary accusations," he said. CBS News reached out to the White House, which referred us to a statement from Steven Cheung, who is assistant to the president and White House director of communications. Cheung said the "bull**** Vanity Fair article comes from a book that is complete fiction, and was fabricated from the warped mind of failed spy thriller writer." "He presents no evidence or even a shred of documentation. Just mysterious words from unnamed sources," Cheung said on X. articles.title: Minnesota officials say U.S. government stopped sharing evidence on fatal ICE shootings
articles.summary: A card with images depicting Alex Pretti and Renee Good is placed at a makeshift memorial in Minneapolis, Minnesota, on 28 January 2026. Photograph: Seth Herald/Reuters The federal government has stopped sharing evidence with Minnesota authorities who are investigating the killings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti by federal officers during a violent anti-immigration, anti-protest crackdown in the state earlier this year, state officials said in recent court filings. Minnesota officials sued the Trump administration in March for access to materials they said they needed to independently investigate the shootings. The family of Good, 37, earlier this month sued over her death when she was shot by a federal officer with Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) as she drove her car away during a protest in January. Pretti, also 37 , was shot dead in the street by a border patrol agent as he went to the assistance of a fellow protester on the icy city streets during fierce demonstrations against the crackdown. Both Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and ICE are under the umbrella of the Department of Homeland Security. The shootings of the two protesters, both US citizens, was a turning point in the government’s approach after weeks of violent action by ranks of militarized, masked federal immigration enforcement in Minneapolis, which local leaders called a siege , after months of similar mass operations in major cities. Related: Minneapolis leaders call the ICE surge a ‘siege’. My reporting from there concurs There were immediate disputes over the investigations into Good’s and later Pretti’s killings between state and federal authorities. The Trump administration has suggested that state prosecutors don’t have jurisdiction to investigate federal officers, while Minnesota officials have said they don’t trust the federal government to investigate itself. The state is still seeking the cellphones of the officers involved in both shootings and recordings of key interviews. State prosecutors announced in July that the federal government had begun turning over evidence in the cases, including police body-camera video and hard drives containing statements. The Hennepin county attorney, Mary Moriarty, said at the time that the state expected to receive “all the evidence”. But Minnesota investigators said in October court filings that the transfer of evidence stopped soon after the July announcement. Moriarty said the US attorney’s office for Minnesota, the state outpost of federal prosecutors, told her on 10 September that evidence sharing would be on pause indefinitely “in light of challenges with DC”, according to the documents, referring to Washington and the federal authorities. State prosecutors have again asked a judge to order federal agencies to hand over the evidence, arguing they “have identified no legal authority or rational basis justifying their obstruction of state criminal investigations”. In a reply filed on Tuesday, attorneys for the US justice department argued it was within their discretion to decline to share information with state authorities. Drew Evans, superintendent of the Minnesota bureau of criminal apprehension, said in a legal declaration that federal authorities still have Good’s clothing, the cellphone of the officer who killed her and interview recordings that state authorities have never been able to view. Bystanders captured footage of the shooting death of Good in her car and Pretti on the street , in each case contradicting key parts of what the administration said prompted the killings. No criminal charges have been filed. Evans said the federal government also has not shared a recorded statement from an officer who shot Pretti, the firearms used by the officers, their phones, projectiles and casings. articles.title: Meghan Markle says she was 'deeply distressed' by allegations against her father
articles.summary: Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has said she is "deeply distressed" by the news that her father, Thomas Markle, is under investigation over claims he possessed images containing child sexual abuse in his home. The images were reportedly found in his home in the Philippines after he returned to the U.S. in May, Philippine officials said. Thomas Markle has denied the allegations, calling them "sick lies" and "the worst thing anyone could accuse me of." In a statement through her spokesperson, Meghan Markle has said that she is "deeply distressed" by the news, and that she was first made aware of the claims by the Met Police in 2018. "I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed," Meghan's statement said. "In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan police and Royalty and Specialist Protection. That letter was subsequently shared with me. It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated. "I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications' distortion over the years, any distance from my father, and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them. "I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families. "Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children." The allegations, reported by Mail Online , said Thomas Markle is under investigation after being reported by his son, Thomas Markle Jr. In a statement to Mail Online , the elder Markle said: "I'm shocked, I'm hurt and I'm very upset that my son is making these accusations against me. I could never do what I'm being accused of. It's the worst thing anyone could accuse me of. He added: "It's just a bunch of lies. It's sick. I have no idea why Tom [Markle] is trying to destroy me with these lies." Yahoo has contacted the Met Office and authorities in the U.S. and the Philippines for comment. articles.title: President Trump unveils renovated Reflecting Pool with anti-vandal cameras
articles.summary: President Donald Trump said Friday that the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is continuing to fill with water, declaring that the landmark is “looking really good” and will be protected by anti-vandalism cameras. The pool has become a recurring point of attention since Trump ordered it resurfaced in “American flag blue” ahead of the nation’s 250th anniversary celebrations. The project has faced rising costs, algae issues, and damage to its freshly installed lining. Trump shared an image of the Reflecting Pool on the Truth Social platform on Friday. In a message posted to Truth Social in the early hours of Friday morning, Trump said the Reflecting Pool was 85 percent full, “and looking really good!” Trump added: “It hasn’t worked properly since 1922, but will now. We have cameras set up to stop any potential Vandalism, including the grassed areas, which were destroyed by chemical poisoning with a large, and very inappropriate, phrase. The grass was completely replaced!” The president also included in his post an image the Reflecting Pool on the National Mall, with the Lincoln Memorial centered in the distance. Newsweek reached out to the White House for comment via email on Friday. Cases Dropped Trump earlier this week threatened any potential vandals with jail time, reviving a dispute over cause of damage to the pool’s lining. A judge dismissed a case against former Olympian canoeist David Hearn this month, and federal prosecutors previously moved to dismiss the case after records suggested that a flawed installation, rather than vandalism, were to blame for the damage. Doug Buchanan, director of media and public relations for DC Courts, told Newsweek previously that he believed “there were three or four additional [vandalism] cases filed–but dismissed by the USAO/DC [U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia] before the cases made it to court.” Trump also alleged this week that grass near the pool had been “scarred by poison” with the numbers “86 47” , and said the turf had since been replaced. Algae, Peeling and Vandalism Claims Trump announced renovations in April , ahead of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of American independence. The project involved resurfacing the bottom of the pool with a blue coating Trump described as “American flag blue.” NBC News reported that Trump initially estimated the work would cost between $1.5 million and $2 million and take one to two weeks, but that its cost subsequently rose to around $16 million. Problems emerged shortly after the pool was refilled . Its water turned green amid an algae bloom, while sections of the newly installed coating began to peel. Footage published by Newsweek in June showed the water changing color soon after the refurbishment, despite the pool’s new blue finish. A further contract was later awarded for renovation and maintenance work intended to tackle the algae, Newsweek reported previously . Trump has repeatedly attributed damage to vandals . Federal prosecutors said in a motion to dismiss Hearn’s case that records obtained from the Interior Department documented repeated failures of the lining during its installation and extensive peeling across the pool. The filing also pointed to pressure to complete the project before July 4. The Reflecting Pool has undergone major work before. A two-year reconstruction completed in 2012 addressed longstanding sinking and leakage, adding more than 2,000 supporting pilings and a circulation system drawing water from the nearby Tidal Basin, according to Histories of the National Mall. articles.title: Melania Trump secures ceasefire in Russian-held Ukrainian city, White House says
articles.summary: First lady Melania Trump (Finn Gomez/Getty Images) First lady Melania Trump has successfully negotiated a temporary ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine to allow humanitarian aid and civilian evacuations in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky, her senior adviser, Marc Beckman, revealed for the first time Friday on Newsmax's " National Report ." Appearing live in the Newsmax studio, Beckman disclosed that representatives of both countries had signed the agreement just hours before his appearance, marking a significant humanitarian breakthrough in the nearly five-year war. "Let me start by being very crystal clear: the first lady of the United States of America has successfully negotiated a ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia, localized in this region of Oleshky," Beckman told Newsmax. The ceasefire, scheduled to begin Oct. 29, will allow Ukrainian and Russian civilian representatives to enter Oleshky, about 5 miles behind the front lines, to identify residents needing assistance and coordinate evacuations, Beckman said. "It will bring humanitarian aid to the entire city, this includes medics, medicine, food, clean water," he said, noting the operation will include "an evacuation of the city of Oleshky as well." Newsmax has been granted exclusive television access to accompany a delegation of Russian and Ukrainian observers entering Oleshky on Oct. 29. Both Ukrainian and Russian officials agreed to allow Newsmax to document the humanitarian operation. Beckman emphasized the immediacy of the breakthrough, revealing that the agreement had only just been finalized. "As recently as this morning, I'm coming here, and the ink is still wet on the paper," he said. He said the agreement had been signed just hours before his Newsmax appearance. "So you're the first to know," Beckman said. Residents Facing Starvation Oleshky, located in southern Ukraine's Kherson region, had about 24,000 residents before Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Fewer than 2,000 residents remain, primarily elderly civilians unable to escape, along with approximately 50 children. Conditions have deteriorated dramatically, with residents facing severe food shortages, limited electricity, no running water, and no heat. Roads around Oleshky are reportedly heavily mined and targeted by armed drones. One route connecting Oleshky with nearby Radensk has become known as the "Road of Death" because it is littered with destroyed vehicles. Beckman described an increasingly desperate humanitarian emergency. "They're eating weeds and grass," he told Newsmax, describing reports of civilians struggling to survive. In a statement released Friday, Melania Trump said her intervention was essential to prevent further suffering. "The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster," the first lady said. "Oleshky's remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water." "It was abundantly clear that without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible." Beckman revealed on Newsmax that the negotiations began after the first lady learned about Oleshky's humanitarian crisis during her Fostering the Future Together event held in conjunction with the United Nations General Assembly in September. Her earlier efforts to reunite children separated from their families during the war helped establish direct communication channels with Russian and Ukrainian leaders. The first lady has helped facilitate the reunification of 34 Ukrainian and Russian children with their families since the war began. "Both sides formally recognized her as an intermediary and in writing, and they gave her the power to negotiate this ceasefire," Beckman said. Beckman said the first lady spent more than a month negotiating with both governments to finalize the agreement. The first lady said representatives from both countries will visit residents in their homes, assess their needs, and arrange transportation for those wishing to leave. "Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination," Trump said. "I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine." Newsmax cameras will document the operation, providing independent visibility into the evacuation process and whether residents' wishes are respected. A Possible Step Toward Peace Although the agreement is limited to Oleshky and does not establish a broader ceasefire, Beckman expressed hope that it could lead to further diplomatic progress. "Indeed, in my opinion, this is the first step towards everlasting peace between these two nations," he said. Beckman said Ukrainian and Russian representatives were enthusiastic when signing the agreement, saying both countries' presidents had supported the first lady's efforts. Nevertheless, he cautioned against assuming the humanitarian breakthrough would immediately produce a comprehensive peace agreement. "My hope is that this ceasefire... creates a better peace within the region for Europe," Beckman said. For now, the immediate priority remains delivering desperately needed supplies and providing a safe passage out of Oleshky. The unprecedented arrangement puts Melania Trump at the center of a rare cooperative humanitarian effort between the warring nations Important: Download the free Newsmax App on your smartphone and get latest updates from Ukraine, Russia and our breaking news! articles.title: Elon Musk is preparing for a Democratic Congress and warns he'll fight back
articles.summary: Elon Musk has adopted a war posture in response to looming threats of congressional investigations: If Democrats win control of Congress in next month’s midterm elections, Musk has signaled he is bracing for a fight. “Live by the sword, die by the sword,” he said Wednesday in a post on X, responding to a Politico report that cited Democratic lawmakers seeking to investigate him. Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post. “Those who pick fights with me should understand that I will find out who is really pulling the strings and come for them, not just their puppets,” said Musk, the CEO of Tesla and SpaceX. Musk’s battle-ready stance comes as a host of Democrats have said they are eager to wield the power of their office to investigate the world’s richest person should they win either chamber in the midterms. As Republicans’ election prospects have soured, lawmakers are building momentum for probes looking into the tech mogul, his companies or the work of the U.S. DOGE Service, which Musk oversaw and which was instrumental in dismantling the U.S. Agency for International Development. Sen. Richard Blumenthal (Connecticut), the ranking Democrat on the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, said in an interview Thursday that he would investigate Musk and DOGE if Democrats win. Blumenthal led inquiries relating to the cost-cutting group but was in the minority and did not have subpoena power, which could be used to compel the attendance of witnesses, as well as the production of documents and records. “The American people have a right to know the cost, the consequences and the chaos resulting from DOGE and … what he may be concealing,” Blumenthal said. “There is a web of potential corruption here that needs to be explored.” He dismissed Musk’s threats of retaliation, expressing surprise at his strong reaction. “He should have nothing to hide,” said Blumenthal, adding that he would expect a Democratic chair of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee to support efforts to investigate Musk. Musk did not respond to requests for comment. Diverging from many of his corporate peers, Musk has consistently countered threats with force. He has contested lawsuits, picked fights with powerful government officials and at times taken drastic action over business disputes, including changing his state of residence - and the locations of his businesses - from California to Texas. But Musk has also acknowledged his own vulnerability in an unfavorable political environment, joking in 2024 about the prospect of going to prison if President Donald Trump was not elected to a second term. Musk has also poured his resources into midterm races, eclipsing his donations toward Trump’s election in 2024. He is the largest individual donor in the 2026 midterm elections, putting more than $350 million toward efforts to elect Republicans. Musk and others who carried out DOGE’s agenda face a potential slew of subpoenas, investigations and hearings after the midterms, in which Democrats are heavily favored. Several other Democratic members of Congress have also raised the prospect of exploring Musk’s business or political ventures in recent days. Rep. James Walkinshaw (D-Virginia), a member of the House Oversight Committee, tagged Musk in a post on X. “I’d just like you to explain to Congress and the American people why DOGE failed so miserably and why you then lied about the savings,” he wrote. “Will you commit to testifying under oath to explain?” Disputed legacy As an influential adviser to President Donald Trump last year, Musk oversaw the sweeping and at times chaotic U.S. DOGE Service campaign to cut costs at government agencies. Staffed largely with young tech workers new to government service who were chosen by Musk and his circle, DOGE eliminated the jobs of hundreds of thousands of federal workers and accessed sensitive data on hundreds of millions of Americans. Musk said that he aimed to cut $2 trillion in federal spending with DOGE, which ultimately claimed $215 billion in estimated savings. A Government Accountability Office audit found that the group consistently overstated its savings. DOGE took credit for lease cancellations set into motion before it existed, for example, and claimed savings from contracts that continued to exist. Musk has at times issued threats of retribution on X, the platform he bought in 2022 when it was named Twitter and later folded into his rocket company SpaceX. “There is a large graveyard filled with my enemies,” he wrote in a 2023 post. “I do not wish to add to it, but will if given no choice. Those who pick fights with me do so at their own peril, but maybe this is their lucky day.” The entrepreneur mused about his fate if Democrats took power in a 2024 interview with Tucker Carlson. “If he loses, I’m f---ed,” Musk said, going on to joke: “How long do you think my prison sentence is going to be?” “There may be some vengeance on me” if Trump doesn’t retake the White House, Musk said in the interview, which took place before the election. Should Democrats regain control of Congress this time, they will face pressure from some voters and activist groups to move on Musk. Activist group Investigate DOGE has channeled the spirit of the Tesla Takedown movement, which staged anti-Musk demonstrations outside Tesla showrooms, calling for Musk and DOGE alumni to face congressional scrutiny. Activists are asking, “‘How do we make sure Elon gets held accountable if Democrats take congress again?’” said Evan Sutton, a spokesman for the group. “Congress needs to get in there. They need to get their hands dirty. The American people need to know what happened.” Some former DOGE staffers are already taking precautions in the event of a Democratic-controlled Congress, seeking to insulate themselves from the potential outcomes of ethics probes by attempting to button up their post-DOGE business dealings. Though the midterms are still more than a week away, Musk continues to signal he’s readying a counteroffensive. Responding to a video of the tech journalist Kara Swisher noting that if Democrats take power, he “knows what’s coming,” Musk had a simple reply: “Message received.” Related Content This article originally appeared on Washington Post at https://washingtonpost.com/technology/2026/10/23/musk-says-he-will-fight-back-if-congressional-democrats-investigate-doge/

articles.title: Trump admin. seeks to block Alaska Senate result if Dan Sullivan narrowly loses
articles.summary: The Trump administration aims to stop Alaska from certifying the Senate race result if Republican Senator Dan Sullivan loses to Democrat Mary Peltola and votes for another candidate named Dan Sullivan could have changed the outcome. A lawsuit filed by the Department of Justice (DOJ) on Thursday against the state of Alaska and various election officials alleges that the Republican candidate listed on the ballot as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. entered the race intending to mislead voters into backing him instead of the incumbent with the same name. President Donald Trump has repeatedly accused Democrats of planting Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher, to confuse Alaska voters. In a social media post earlier this week, Trump—who has endorsed the incumbent—called his presence on the ballot a “scam” that could threaten Senator Dan Sullivan’s potential victory in what has become one of the closest Senate contests this year. “Even 1, 2, or 3 percent could make the difference,” the president wrote. “Dan S. Sullivan is leading by a lot, but this is CHEATING in an Election, and the Judge that allowed this to happen should be ashamed of himself.” Senator Dan Sullivan is currently 2.7 points behind Peltola, according to VoteHub’s poll tracker , underscoring how potentially consequential even a small number of votes could be. President Donald Trump speaks at a campaign rally at Sioux Gateway Airport, Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026, in Sioux City, Iowa. Dan J. Sullivan was a member of the Alaska Independence Party until it dissolved late last year, only registering as a Republican when he filed his candidacy in the Senate race earlier this year. Alaska election officials initially agreed that the retired teacher’s filing was intended to confuse voters and sought to exclude him from the ballot. But an Alaska trial court ruled against that exclusion and the Alaska Supreme Court summarily affirmed that decision, putting Dan J. Sullivan back on the ballot. The lawsuit hinges on whether the votes cast for the “decoy” Sullivan, a retired teacher, would have changed the winner under Alaska’s ranked choice voting system if they had instead been cast for the Trump-endorsed incumbent. It would also require an investigation into whether Alaskans who cast their vote for Dan J. Sullivan actually intended to vote for the incumbent, and it would allow further procedures to determine what the election result would have been without the alleged voter confusion. This photo taken with a smartphone, voters stand in line at an early voting location in a mall in Anchorage, Alaska, on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. Newsweek contacted the White House, the DOJ, Alaska Division of Elections, Peltola’s and both Sullivans’ campaigns for comment by email on Friday morning, outside of standard working hours. What Election Experts Think of the DOJ Lawsuit “The lawsuit is based on very real and valid concerns about voter confusion,” Michael Morley, the Sheila M. McDevitt Professor of Law and Faculty Director of the Election Law Center at the Florida State University, told Newsweek . “The Alaska secretary of state concluded Daniel J. Sullivan is not an actual good-faith candidate but rather was running only to confuse or mislead voters. Having said that, the DOJ’s lawsuit is completely meritless,” he added. The DOJ sued under the National Voter Registration Act, Morley said, but does not even allege that the statute has been violated here. “Rather, the DOJ is claiming that allowing the election’s results to be impacted by a sham candidacy would undermine the law’s purpose. That’s not a valid basis for suing,” the professor said. “Moreover, any concerns about the sham candidacy could have been raised before the election, before votes were cast. Indeed, Alaska courts refused to allow election officials to remove him from the ballot,” Morley added. The professor believes the lawsuit will be “quickly” dismissed. “If Senator Dan S. Sullivan loses, and Daniel J. Sullivan’s vote tally exceeds the margin of victory, then the senator’s best bet would be to file an election contest with the U.S. Senate, which is the sole judge of its members’ elections and returns. The Senate can decide for itself whether to accept such results.” Professor Mark Brown, of Capital University School of Law, agrees. “No federal statute authorizes the relief the DOJ seeks and the Alaska Supreme Court has already concluded that Dan J. Sullivan was illegally under Alaska—and federal—law removed from the ballot,” he told Newsweek . “The Alaska Supreme Court thus restored his name to the ballot. DOJ’s lawsuit is frivolous.” Why Are Two Sullivans Running for the Alaska Senate Race? Six years ago, Alaska narrowly passed a ballot measure shifting the state to a ranked choice voting system allowing voters to rank candidates in order of preference. Ballot Measure 2, which got 50.55 percent of the vote in 2020, created the non-partisan pick one primary and the four-candidate ranked choice voting general election that The Last Frontier is now using. President Donald Trump listens as Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, speaks at a campaign rally at the Curtis D. Menard Memorial Sports Center, Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, in Wasilla, Alaska. Under this system, which Alaska shares with only one other state in the country, Maine, the top four candidates from each respective primary in the state earlier this year, whether for governor, the House or the Senate, are set to appear on the ballot on November 3, regardless of party affiliation. Voters have the option to rank them in order of preference, though they can also choose one candidate only if they prefer so. A candidate who receives more than 50 percent of first-choice votes wins outright. If no one passes this threshold, then the candidate who comes in last place is eliminated, and those who selected that candidate first will have their second-choice vote counted. The process continues until one candidate gets more than 50 percent of the vote. This system is why four candidates are on the ballot in the Alaska Senate race, including Democrat Mary Peltola and Republicans Sen. Dan Sullivan, Dan J. Sullivan Jr., and Gerald Heikes. The Trump administration, in the DOJ lawsuit filed Thursday, claimed that “the sole purpose of [Dan J. Sullivan’s] candidacy is to benefit the Peltola campaign by reducing the number of votes for Senator Sullivan.” Dan Sullivan, who has filed to run for U.S. Senate in Alaska, poses for a photo Friday, June 26, 2026, in Petersburg, Alaska. In June, when Dan J. Sullivan was reinstated on the ballot, the retired teacher and fishing enthusiast said that he is running because he is disappointed with Sullivan’s representation and wants change for the state. “It’s a free country,” he said, as reported by Courthouse News Service. “Most Alaskans are proud Independents and it’s my sincere hope that people know who and what they are voting for but ultimately, choice is good and voters’ intent will be as varied as the candidates who are running.” The newly published ballots show that Alaska election officials have come to something of a solution to solve the debate around the two Sullivans. The ballots list incumbent Senator Dan S. Sullivan as a “Registered Republican” and mark him as the “Incumbent.” The retired teacher appears under his full name, “Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.,” without a party designation displayed beneath his name. A Key Race for Control of the Senate Democrats have a chance to seize control of the Senate in the midterms , with Republicans currently holding a narrow 53-47 majority. View embedded content While most of the seats up for grabs in the upper chamber are in states where Trump has won by comfortable margins in 2024, the unpopular war in Iran and rising inflation in recent months have turned many of these races into unexpectedly competitive ones. Alaska, a state which has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 2008, has now become a key battleground in the fight for control of the upper chamber, with Peltola gaining ground over the Republican incumbent. Building on voters’ growing anger over higher prices, Peltola—an Alaskan who supports oil, gas and gun rights—has focused her campaign on the cost of living, trying to appeal to moderate Republicans disappointed with the Trump administration and independents as well as Democrats. Polls show that her strategy may be working. Who Is Leading the Latest Polls? With less than two weeks ahead of Election Day, every poll released this month gives Peltola a narrow but consistent lead over Sullivan, while the other two candidates typically receive less than 5 percent of the vote in the first round. A poll released by progressive pollster Data for Progress earlier this month and conducted between October 8 and October 16 among 675 likely voters, gives Peltola ahead with 49 percent of the vote while Sullivan had 46 percent of the vote in the first round of the election. Dan J. Sullivan had 4 percent of the vote and Heikes only 1 percent. In the final round, Peltola’s lead had grown to 51 percent to Sullivan’s 49 percent. The poll had a margin of error of ±4 percentage points. Alaska U.S. Senate candidate Mary Peltola, a Democrat, speaks during a campaign rally on May 14, 2026, in Juneau, Alaska. The Democratic candidate received 48 percent of the vote in an InsiderAdvantage poll conducted between October 9 and October 10, while Sullivan had 43 percent of the vote in a four-way ballot. Dan J. Sullivan Jr. and Heikes received 1.7 percent and 2.2 percent of the vote, respectively, while 5.3 percent of likely voters were undecided. In the second round of voting, without Dan J. Sullivan and Heikes, 50.1 percent of the vote went to Peltola and 48.0 percent to the incumbent. The poll was conducted among 1,200 likely voters and had margin of error of ±2.83 percentage points. View embedded content Americans Want Trump to Accept Outcome of Midterms A new YouGov survey shows that an overwhelming majority of Americans want the president and his administration to accept the outcome of the midterm elections, no matter the result. According to the poll, conducted on October 22, 2026, among 8,694 U.S. adults, 71 percent of Americans think Trump should “accept the results” if Republicans lose their majority in the U.S. House. The opinion is bipartisan: 87 percent of Democrats, 67 percent of Independents, and 61 percent of Republicans said the same. Only 8 percent of all voters said Trump should not accept the results, while 21 percent said they were not sure. YouGov has not released a similar poll on the Senate. articles.title: Israel shuts down parts of West Bank after shootout kills 2 soldiers and 2 gunmen
articles.summary: JERUSALEM (AP) — Two Israeli soldiers were killed in an attack in the occupied West Bank that also left two suspected gunmen dead Friday morning, the military said. The violence is likely to heighten political tensions and security concerns ahead of next week's parliamentary election . Staff Sgt. Ron Yonatan Roytman, 23, and Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem, 20, were killed and three others were lightly wounded during the attack near the Yehuda Junction outside the West Bank city of Hebron, the army said. The army said its soldiers had prevented a “terror attack against Israeli civilians” and that the two suspects, both Palestinians from Hebron, used an M16 rifle and a handgun. It said the men arrived at an Israeli military position in the morning, triggering an exchange of fire lasting approximately 20 minutes, after which the gunmen were killed by Israeli troops. The army said its forces prevented the men from advancing toward civilians. Netanyahu vows ‘house-by-house’ retaliation Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later visited the attack site as his office instructed security forces to immediately cordon off Hebron and prepare for a full closure of the West Bank, starting Friday. Israel will retaliate with a sweeping anti-terror operation in the Hebron neighborhood where the gunmen lived, Netanyahu said. “We will evacuate the residents, we will go house-by-house, we will also remove the weapons there, and all the terror infrastructure will be dealt with and destroyed,” Netanyahu said. Israeli voters are deciding Tuesday whether to grant Netanyahu yet another term in office — or usher in a new era of Israeli politics three years after Hamas-led attacks triggered the war in Gaza. Israel’s government has warned of potential attacks by the country’s “enemies” in the lead-up to the election. Netanyahu later met with his Security Cabinet and top military and security officials, and blamed Hamas for Friday's attack. “Our brave soldiers thwarted this attack with courage and determination,” he said. “I commend them for their actions and wish our wounded a speedy recovery.” Smotrich urges removing Palestinian Authority control Israel’s national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, known for extremist views , said the attack shows Israel needs to restrict the Palestinians’ freedom of movement in the West Bank. He and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, another far-right member of Netanyahu’s Cabinet, both called for Israel’s military to wrest control of the West Bank from the Palestinian Authority, though there was no evidence Friday to suggest the governing body had any ties to the gunmen. “There is no alternative to a comprehensive military campaign in Judea and Samaria to dismantle the Palestinian Authority, collect the weapons, and eliminate the terrorists, exactly as we did in Gaza and Lebanon,” Smotrich wrote on social media. Within hours, on orders from Smotrich, the Israeli military began demolishing Palestinian-owned buildings surrounding the site of the attack. He called it “establishing deterrence and exacting a price” in a video that appeared to show him at a demolition site, and claimed the buildings set to be torn down were built illegally. Critics say it is nearly impossible to obtain a construction permit from Israel. Dozens are arrested in West Bank security operations Following the shootout, soldiers and Israeli security and intelligence agencies conducted dozens of operations in the West Bank and said they apprehended dozens of people, including those affiliated with Hamas and Islamic Jihad militant groups. The military said it also located weapons, including M16 rifles and submachine guns. Eyal Zamir, the Israeli army’s chief of staff, said a “large quantity of ammunition was found” in a vehicle used by the gunmen. “This ammunition was intended to be used in a larger-scale attack,” he added. Palestinian life is ‘impossible,’ says US congressional candidate Closures of the West Bank are becoming more common. Friday was the fourth time in the past month that Israel imposed restrictions across the territory, shutting gates and checkpoints connecting Palestinian villages to major roads. Roads in the territory remain open to Israeli drivers, including settlers, who can still travel through the area but may face delays. U.S. Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander , who was in the West Bank on Friday, said the army’s response to the attack is an example of Israel enforcing an apartheid system on Palestinians. “It’s part of the effort to take more control, to make Palestinian life impossible,” Lander, who had been detained by Israeli forces on Wednesday, said in an interview. Yishai Fleisher, an international spokesperson for Hebron’s Jewish community and a political candidate for the far-right Otzma Yehudit, or Jewish Power, party, said Israel must defend itself from a “hostile majority.” “We are tired of the weapons and the brainwashing and incitement that is next door,” he said. articles.title: Ramaswamy's Ohio attack ad prompts debate over what's fair game in politics
articles.summary: President Donald Trump's brand of brash, sometimes offensive, politics has consumed the Republican Party for a decade. But bipartisan outrage over Vivek Ramaswamy's ad featuring his opponent's estranged mother shows how candidates often fail when they try to embody the president's bombast. Ramaswamy, an Ohio Republican running for governor against Democrat Amy Acton, a former public health official, gained national prominence as the 2024 presidential candidate who sought to mimic Trump's brand of shock-jock politics, confronting his rivals in public and working the sidelines of social media to rile and excite supporters. Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post. Ramaswamy's newest ad features Acton's mother calling her a "liar," even as documents show that Acton and her brother were removed from her home as children after her stepfather was charged with raping Acton. Political operatives in both parties called the ad an extension of Trump's no-holds-barred politics that catapulted him to the presidency in 2016. Trump's rise was fueled by a Republican ecosystem - much of it online - that has been increasingly shaped in his image over the past decade. And Trump defended Ramaswamy in an online post on Thursday, calling the ad "very powerful" and writing that criticism is meant only to "damage, demean, and embarrass a Republican." "I told him leave it up and look upstairs and say 'thank you, God, very much, I appreciate it,'" Trump said at a rally in Iowa on Thursday night, recounting a conversation he said he had with Ramaswamy urging him to keep the ad up. But the swift bipartisan blowback the ad has received suggests there are limits to the party's attack-first strategy, both now and potentially when Trump eventually steps off the stage in 2028. Mike DeWine, Ohio's outgoing Republican governor, on Thursday became the latest, and perhaps most significant, figure to denounce the ad, which began airing this week. "The ad, on its face, is deeply, deeply troubling," said DeWine, who endorsed Ramaswamy. "It's wrong to run this ad." That echoed comments made Wednesday by Sen. Jon Husted, a Republican whose reelection campaign is pivotal to his party's hopes of holding on to Senate control. "I would not have run that ad," Husted said. The string of high-profile denunciations has introduced a level of panic in a red state where Republicans were already concerned with polls showing they could lose critical races. "The floor may have just fallen out from under the Republican campaign for Ohio Governor," former congressman James B. Renacci, an Ohio Republican who has run for Senate and governor in the state, said in a lengthy overnight post on X Thursday. "And any Republican who fails to distance themselves from this ad risks taking on water as well." Criticism of Ramaswamy came from Republicans outside of the state, too. "It's terrible," Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa), who is locked in a tight contest for the Senate, told ABC News as she called on Ramaswamy to take the ad down. "I think about it as a mom, and you think about your kid surviving childhood sexual abuse and having to relive that trauma on TV again." The blowback to Ramaswamy's ad has not been universal. Ramaswamy has not only defended the spot, but his campaign has pledged to put $4 million behind it. "I would love for this race and this election to be about the substantive issues that impact Ohioans. Unfortunately, Amy Acton has been hiding from those issues," he told reporters earlier this week. The Ramaswamy campaign decided to put money behind the ads after testing with focus groups showed they were effective, a person briefed on the research told The Washington Post, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss internal strategy. Vice President JD Vance, while campaigning in Ohio on Wednesday, said he was "a little bit disgusted" by Republicans who were "whining more about that advertisement than they are about what the congressional Democrats and other Democrats want to do to the United States of America." And Shannon Burns, head of one of the state's largest Republican organizations, said the ad has "lit a fuse under a dormant base." "No matter what the talking heads say or the people who are clutching their pearls say, the Republican base is what matters for Vivek to win," Burns said. "If the Republican base turns out, we win." Polls show that voters are disheartened by the tone of American politics, including Republicans who have backed Trump. A Gallup survey released late last year found 69 percent of Americans believe the Republican Party and Republicans have gone too far with the use of inflammatory language to attack their opponents, while 60 percent believe the same of Democrats and the Democratic Party. "Our politics is a reflection of us, and I think that is where we are at as a country, and so our campaigns are reflecting that," said Jason Savage, a longtime Republican operative in Maine who used to run the Maine Republican Party. He argued that too many Republican candidates try "to replicate something they saw before." "People don't really need you to be Donald Trump," Savage said. "They need you to be you." This question is particularly potent for Vance, who is openly considering a 2028 campaign and has embraced much of Trump's style. "Politics is a tough business," Vance said, while publicly reflecting on the ad. Vance's response angered Republicans who may run against him in 2028. "Vice President Vance said today that whether this ad by Vivek Ramaswamy was appropriate was not really his concern," Chris Christie, the former governor of New Jersey and a possible 2028 candidate, told The Post. "Seriously?" Christie added: "Vance's acceptance of this campaign ad only breathes life into the disease that we should be seeking to cure." Another person formerly close to Trump said the ad was among the clearest examples of the pitfalls of mimicking Trump. "Trump is an aberration in American politics. So even if it has been successful for him … I am not sure it is readily transferrable to other people," said John Bolton, a longtime Republican figure who served in Trump's first term before breaking with the president. Because Trump's movement is based more on personality than a set of unifying issues, there is little for his successors to grasp beyond his style, he said. "There really isn't an -ism to pass on," Bolton said. Some Republicans argued that Trump's brand of politics often only works when the political environment is behind him. He is now at his lowest ebb in polls, which show deep anger toward Trump over the economy and high gas prices. In 2016, his bluster met an electorate frustrated by eight years of Democratic control of the White House and the prospect that a second politician from the same family, Hillary Clinton, might become president. In 2024, Trump's constant attacks on President Joe Biden and Democratic nominee Kamala Harris met a restive electorate that felt the Democratic administration was telling them the economy was strong and didn't understand the pain of high prices. "But the problem unique to this cycle is that nobody cares about a politician having sharp elbows and 'owning the libs' when they can't even afford groceries, a tank of gas and other basic necessities," said a Republican operative involved in multiple races who spoke on the condition of anonymity to speak candidly about his party's candidates. Isaac Arnsdorf contributed to this report. articles.title: Supreme Court sides with Republicans in New Hampshire student ID voting fight
articles.summary: WASHINGTON – The Supreme Court said New Hampshire can fully enforce a ban on voters using student IDs as a form of identification at the polls next month, a win for the Republican Party's effort to tighten voting procedures. The court on Oct. 22 agreed to pause a lower court’s ruling that a student ID is among the forms of identification that may be considered by poll workers if the voter lacks an approved government-issued ID. The state's U.S. Senate race is among the contests that will decide whether Republicans keep control of that chamber after the midterm elections. The Republican National Committee had backed the state's unsuccessful emergency appeal to the Supreme Court . New Hampshire, controlled by Republicans, is among several states that have banned registered voters from using a student ID to verify their identity at the polls. A voting-rights group challenged the change as discrimination against younger voters and as an unconstitutional burden on their right to vote. A federal judge in New Hampshire declined to block enforcement of the law as the case is litigated. But the judge also said the new law had not changed the fact that a poll worker may accept or reject a student ID as a valid form of identification on a case-by-case basis through the state’s "safety-valve" provision. New Hampshire Secretary of State David Scanlan asked the Supreme Court to intervene. Scanlan, a Republican, said the judge's Oct. 2 order injected uncertainty into the state’s voting procedures less than three weeks before the election. He also said the judge wrongly interpreted the state's law. Coalition for Open Democracy, the group challenging the law, said the judge correctly concluded that state officials failed to identify "any security or integrity concerns specific to student ID cards and why they are unique among other non-governmental forms of identification" that are allowed on a case-by-case basis. The judge also found that the change had already kept one student from voting and could affect more because young voters may not have the government-issued IDs that are automatically accepted. In the brief and unsigned opinion, the Supreme Court pointed to its previous rulings that federal courts should not alter rules on the eve of an election. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson was the only justice to publicly disagree with that decision. She said the federal judge had not changed the rules but only corrected the secretary of state's misinterpretation of them. "I respectfully dissent because − even, and perhaps especially, when an election is looming − I would not disturb aclearly justifiable federal-court order issued to ensure that the public receives accurate information about a State'selectoral processes," she wrote. articles.title: 从CoreWeave到Anthropic，芯片抵押融资正重塑AI债务市场
articles.summary: 以芯片为抵押物的结构性融资，正在成为全球AI扩张的核心资金引擎，并迅速发展为一个规模可能突破万亿美元的全新资产类别。 这一市场的雏形始于2023年黑石向CoreWeave提供的一笔23亿美元私募信贷，成为芯片抵押债务的首单标志性交易。 如今，博通正与华尔街机构磋商为Anthropic安排600亿美元芯片融资，SpaceX据报正寻求为英伟达芯片融资400亿美元，英伟达本身亦宣布与六大贷款机构达成5000亿美元合作框架。 摩根大通分析师预计，2030年前芯片支出总额或超3万亿美元，其中大部分将依赖举债融资。 然而，这场债务扩张也带来不容忽视的风险。由于交易多为私募性质，投资者缺乏便捷的退出渠道；芯片厂商、云计算巨头与新兴云服务商之间的交叉敞口高度集中。 CoreWeave企业层面的垃圾级债券近期大幅下挫，部分跌至面值80美分，收益率攀升至约15%，折射出市场对AI商业回报的深层疑虑。 一笔融资开创新范式 这场革命的起点，是黑石战术机遇团队对一个陌生概念的审慎评估。据当时参与尽调的CoreWeave联合创始人Brannin McBee回忆，黑石高管当年曾直接发问："什么是GPU？""AI是真实存在的吗？" 获得满意答案后，黑石于2023年主导完成了对CoreWeave的23亿美元私募信贷，开创了芯片抵押债务融资的先例。 这一结构的核心逻辑在于： 成立特殊目的载体（SPV）购买并持有芯片，以目标客户合同产生的现金流偿还债务，债务期限与芯片五至六年的折旧周期相匹配，从而将硬件贬值风险锁定在可预测范围之内。 CoreWeave的模式脱胎于商品市场经验——类似液化天然气领域"先签合同、再融资建厂"的开发模式。首笔交易以微软合同为抵押，彼时融资成本高达中双位数利率水平，McBee坦言这是他"职业生涯中最艰难的一次尽调"。 随着CoreWeave客户阵容持续扩大，其融资成本随之下降。今年3月，公司以Meta合同为支撑完成85亿美元债务融资，借款利率降至约6%——华尔街按照Meta的高评级而非CoreWeave自身的垃圾评级来定价风险。 芯片成本远超数据中心 理解这场融资革命的规模，需要首先理解芯片支出的量级。芯片造价是容纳它们的数据中心的两至四倍，却在五至六年内折旧殆尽，由此形成了传统资本市场难以独立消化的巨额融资缺口。 以AI云服务商Nscale在西弗吉尼亚州的旗舰项目为例，配套发电厂预计耗资65亿美元，数据中心及设备造价180亿美元，而GPU采购成本则高达470亿美元。 Alphabet旗下谷歌、微软、亚马逊、Meta等投资级云计算巨头可借助充裕现金或廉价债券融资覆盖上述硬件成本，但OpenAI、Anthropic及一众新兴云服务商并不具备这样的资产负债表实力。 OpenAI业务财务官Mike Liberatore坦言："基础设施建设规模史无前例。没有任何剧本告诉你，如何在极度资本密集的情况下，用传统方式从零走向通用人工智能。" 为此，业界移植了项目融资与结构性融资的机制：通过SPV将每笔交易风险隔离，以交易本身的质量和客户信用而非发行人自身评级为基础举债，往往不计入企业资产负债表。 芯片厂商直接入场背书 博通与英伟达的深度介入，将这一市场推向了新的量级。两家公司为相关债务交易提供"兜底"承诺： 一旦借款方违约，芯片将被重新租赁或出售以偿还剩余债务，芯片厂商负责填补缺口。这一机制使SPV发行的优先级债券能够与芯片厂商的投资级评级挂钩，显著压低融资成本。 Apollo与黑石近期联合完成了一笔350亿美元的"Big Sky"交易，为Anthropic提供支持。这也是博通、Apollo与黑石联合搭建的"AI XPV"平台首单落地交易——美国银行策略师估算，该平台若实现20吉瓦的融资容量，至2029年中期或需2350亿美元有背书债务。 在此次Anthropic交易中，博通提供兜底支持的两只优先级债券获得投资级评级，最大一档利率为5.75%；风险较高的45亿美元次级档定价8.5%——仍远低于Anthropic作为未评级私营公司的独立融资成本。 今年8月，英伟达更集结了Apollo、黑石、贝莱德、Brookfield、KKR及高盛，共同为AI基础设施提供融资来源，英伟达本身承诺兜底其中最高25%的份额。 从私募走向银团市场 要实现真正意义上的规模化，芯片融资必须突破私募市场的边界，进入银团贷款乃至投资级公开债券市场——后者是全球规模最大、成本最低的资本池之一。 CoreWeave今年率先完成了芯片支持的银团杠杆贷款，两笔交易均获机构投资者稳健认购，在市场上交易价格接近面值，与同一公司的企业级债券形成鲜明对比。 摩根士丹利结构性产品与私募资本市场全球负责人Rich Myers表示："这些融资与市场上最具价值的资产直接挂钩，也就是芯片所产生的算力。大量证据表明，算力需求将持续增长，且超过算力供应。" Apollo全球资产配置负责人Chris Edson则表示，传统公开债务市场无法独力满足数字基础设施的融资规模，需要项目融资、私募配售、保险资金及商业房地产等多类资本参与。获得投资级评级，是打开保险资金等最大资本池的关键钥匙。 风险积聚不容忽视 然而，随着资本加速涌入，风险也在同步积聚。 Fitch Ratings高级董事Jason Pompeii指出，当前的厂商融资规模前所未有，且风险高度集中。"这只会增加一种可能性：一旦AI最终令人失望，整条供应链都将受到冲击。" 交易结构的私募性质导致流动性存疑。由于大多数芯片融资交易不在公开市场流通，投资者难以便捷退出，而交易将少数芯片厂商、云计算巨头与新兴云服务商深度绑定，交叉敞口高度集中。Magnetar替代信贷与固定收益业务董事总经理Dave Snyderman警告："巨头只会更大。只有他们才能获得融资渠道。" 客户合同的法律效力同样存在疑问。Carlyle资产支持融资负责人Akhil Bansal直言："所有人都假设这些合同牢不可破，但我关注的是现实层面——如果只有七家机构为GPU提供所有信用支持，筹码究竟在谁手里？" Nuveen私募固定收益负责人Laura Parrott则表示，她目前暂缓参与大型投资级芯片交易，待市场结构更为成熟后再行评估。"这是一种全新结构，一旦出现某种冲击，我们尚不清楚结果会如何演变。" 此外，宏观层面的变数同样存在：德克萨斯州的地方反对势力已促成新项目暂停令，甲骨文在新墨西哥州的项目受监管阻碍被迫推迟付款，OpenAI与Anthropic也在就安全问题讨论放缓部署节奏。 迈向"算力资产类别" 尽管挑战并存，市场参与者对这一范式的长期潜力仍持乐观态度。 黑石战术机遇团队高级董事总经理John Watson将当前时刻比作汽车行业的早期岁月：当年为福特T型车提供融资的人同样面临"人们真的会开车吗"的疑问，如今汽车金融已发展为规模庞大、运作成熟的市场。 在芯片市场演进层面，早期研究与实际使用数据显示，芯片的实际使用寿命正超出当前会计处理所体现的年限，这将改善其可融资性。美国银行基础设施与可持续融资全球负责人Karen Fang预计，类似二手车价格指南的半导体估值工具将逐步出现，进而催生更活跃的芯片租赁与对冲市场。 Watson描绘的终极愿景是：将一个算力单位转化为可在全球范围内交易和融资的资产类别——"我们理解算力的经济价值，因而为它融资。" 实现这一目标，仍有赖于AI商业化进程真正兑现市场预期。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: AI股遭遇DeepSeek时刻以来最惨一跌！高盛动量组合抹去全年涨幅，半导体指数逼近年线
articles.summary: AI动能交易正急转直下。曾在6月一度累计上涨约70%的高贝塔动能组合，如今已悉数回吐年内涨幅；费城半导体指数（SOX）在过去9个交易日相对标普500指数的表现，更创下逾20年来最差纪录。 10月23日，市场对AI投资回报的疑虑进一步升温。 高盛交易台将本轮AI及半导体板块的集中抛售称为“自DeepSeek冲击日以来最差表现”，Meta财报引发的AI投入成本与回报之争，成为本轮跌势加速的催化剂。 抛售正在从股价层面蔓延至投资组合。高盛Prime数据显示，对冲基金基本面多空净杠杆率已降至过去一年的第1百分位，全球AI股票多空比也跌至第6百分位；与此同时，瑞银数据显示，系统性策略的做空杠杆率已升至过去五年的第99百分位。 市场风格也随之转变。随着高贝塔动能交易退潮，低波动与盈利质量因子重新走强， 资金开始从追逐高弹性资产转向更注重防御性与盈利确定性的策略 。AI交易能否重新获得支撑，取决于市场对巨额资本支出回报的重新评估。 年内涨幅悉数归零，动能交易遭遇重挫 数据显示，高盛高贝塔动能配对组合（GS High Beta Momentum Pair）在6月峰值时年内涨幅一度达到约70%，截至10月已将涨幅全部回吐。 无约束动能策略（Unconstrained Momentum）也正经历全球金融危机以来最严重的回撤，仅次于疫情冲击期间。 高盛交易台表示，上周四，前期强势股再度遭遇集中抛售，AI及半导体板块表现尤为疲弱。Meta财报加剧了市场对AI资本支出回报率的疑虑，投资者开始重新权衡巨额投入能否转化为相应收益。 半导体板块的跌势尤其突出。据Peter Callahan的数据， 自10月12日起的9个交易日内，SOX相对标普500下跌约13%，创下逾20年来同等时间窗口内的最大相对跌幅，处于历史分布的第1百分位。 持续下跌也将SOX推至200日移动均线附近，这是该指数自2025年6月以来首次触及这一关键技术位置。 该均线能否提供支撑，将成为观察半导体板块调整是否进一步深化的重要指标。 对冲基金加速去风险，做空杠杆升至高位 据高盛Prime数据，基本面多空净杠杆率本月下降3.1个百分点至49.4%，处于过去一年分布的第1百分位、过去三年的第4百分位， 显示对冲基金正在显著压缩净市场敞口。 全球AI股票多空比已降至过去一年的第6百分位，动能因子敞口也跌至2025年6月下旬以来的最低水平。不过，从五年历史分布看，动能因子敞口仍处于第73百分位，尚未降至长期低位。 做空端则持续升温。 据瑞银数据，系统性策略的做空杠杆率已接近过去五年高位，处于第99百分位。 但做多杠杆率也升至第94百分位，说明多空两端的杠杆均处于高位，市场并非单纯转向单边看空，而是正在重新调整仓位与风险敞口。 低波动与盈利质量走强，资金转向防御 随着高贝塔动能交易退潮，低波动因子近期表现强势，重新成为资金青睐的配置方向；盈利质量因子同样走强。据高盛Prime数据，其敞口已升至过去五年高位。 高盛交易台指出，在行业、板块和因子中性调整后，高盛质量指数过去三个月上涨约20%，相当于约13倍波动率的表现，主要受低质量股票大幅跑输推动。 这一变化表明，资金正从追逐高增长、高弹性的资产，转向更看重盈利质量与业绩确定性的标的。随着投资者重新评估AI资本支出的成本、回报及兑现周期，相关资产的估值重估可能仍将持续。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: Agent、机器人与制药，谁先被GPT-6 Astra改写？
articles.summary: 回顾9月，AI圈的重磅新闻一个接一个。 9月4日，OpenAI发布GPT-6 Astra。这个发布报告里只字未提机器人的通用模型，转身就空降了机器人评测榜首，甚至让一批机器人Benchmark直接失效。有人半开玩笑地说：机器人领域等了这么多年的“GPT时刻”，居然是GPT自己。 Meta Muse给每个用户配了一台云端电脑，两周就冲上美区App Store榜首；竞争对手Instinct一个月内估值从25亿涨到100亿美元。个人Agent掀起了新一轮烧钱获客大战，可它们能打开的网页，正在一个一个被关上。 AI for Science方面，Claude只用了21小时就找到一种结构像CRISPR的新酶系统ART，AI圈很兴奋，因为AI开始做科学发现了，生物圈的反应则相对平淡，大家想在实验室里验证了再说，为什么会有这种反差现象？ 当模型进化到普通人难以感受到它的进化，研究者的感受是什么样的？本期《硅谷101》，我们请来三位分别站在Agent、机器人和AI制药一线的研究者——Pokee.ai创始人兼CEO朱哲清，破壳机器人创始人、清华大学交叉信息研究院助理教授许华哲，华盛顿大学计算机学院助理教授王晟，一起聊清楚三件事：个人Agent商业化卡在哪？机器人怎么被Astra这样的底层模型冲击？AI制药真正的瓶颈是什么？ 以下是这次对话内容的精选： 前沿科学家视角：GPT-G Astra进化了什么? 泓君：Astra发布后，你们有没有使用过这个产品？或者说我们来看网上的demo，大家觉得最让你惊艳的一个demo是什么？ 许华哲：因为我是做机器人的，我们测了很多Astra在做机器人任务上面的一些能力。我们看到的第一个点就是，它的适应能力非常强。比如说给它某一个机器人本体，让它去做相应的事情，那它很快会发现，这个机器人的运动速度比较快，或者这个机器人的运动空间是怎样的，比如它撞到桌子了，它会说，这个桌子蛮高的，那我是不是应该把手抬得更高一点？ 这其实是把CoT（思维链）这种反思过程的能力，变成一个它实际的动作的能力，这是过去的很多机器人的模型和大模型都不具备的。 另一个是它自我更新、自我升级的能力。因为它有这样的反思，它可以一次一次做同样的事情，每一次做得更好。这个其实在网上大家也看到了，有人拿Astra去操作一个机器人机械臂去画金门大桥，那它第一次画的还是比较差的，但是它画完了以后，它会再想怎么样能画的更好，经过几轮的迭代，它就可以画的非常逼真。 我们试了非常多其他的，比如插花，这是一个经典的机器人任务。我们给它加了一些额外难度，那朵花的茎被劈开两半，有点分叉。这个时候它会知道，因为它分叉了，所以我要捏住这个分叉，把它捏窄一点，再往里塞。这样的能力其实还是比较惊艳的。 泓君：它其实已经理解了一些物理世界操作的规范。 许华哲：我觉得本质上还是理解3D，因为这件事情它还是从三维尺寸层面就可以做出一些理解，但是确实这样的理解已经能够帮助到非常多的非动态的物理世界操作任务了。 泓君：我看网上还有一些很有意思的demo是，他们在用Astra做生成3D的视频，非常的快，然后渲染也很好。 许华哲：这是另一个Astra在机器人方面很令人震惊的能力，就是给它几张图片，它可以很快把图片仿真生成出来。学术圈可能把它叫做Real-to-Sim。这件事过去是需要拍大量的视频照片，需要很多人的手工标定修改。但现在你给Astra这样一个指令，它很快就把整个实验室或者办公室的环境给你复现出来了。那你拿着这样的仿真，可以去训你的机器人，那也会有一个在仿真上面的提升。 朱哲清：我们是做模型公司的，Astra在发布的时候，非常强调他们在后训练、模型开发等等上面的一些迭代能力。试下来以后，并没有那么惊艳，但是它确实在长程任务上面和迭代上面，比之前的几版模型有一个比较稳定的提升。与原来的模型相比，它能够对上下文以及之前完成的任务有更稳定的认知，不会出现太多的幻觉的情况。所以从我们的目前的体验来说还是比较好的。 但可能有几个问题：速度相对来说会慢一些，也有可能跟现在用量很高有关系。同时在更加长程的任务上，比如说让它跑一个晚上，幻觉还是会发生。所以它并没有根本上解决，但总体来说还是提升了不少。 我有朋友同测了一些前端以及设计的任务。从前端的审美跟认知上面，我觉得还是有比较大的提升的。可能是在训练的时候，对于设计和审美方向有特殊的训练有关系。 泓君：Bill，这轮Astra的发布，你觉得从模型对行业的影响来看，它跟当年opus 4.6、4.7的发布，从Coding能力的进化来比，它是一个大的节点吗？ 朱哲清：单纯Coding来说，可能没有那么大的一个节点。4.5到4.6，当时我们的体感是一个几乎范式式的转变，原来只能依赖它做短程Coding，几个file的改动，做一些简单的小项目，到4.6那一次模型以后，基本上你会感受到工具调用几乎不会出错了，它去做一些长程的Coding任务，可以自主进行了。 而现在Astra 只是说可以做到更长程的任务，幻觉是可以降更低，审美变得更好。但它没有做到说，我能够解决一个完全以前完全解决不了的问题。 王晟：我觉得是一个大的节点。我们现在已经都从之前Claude等系列模型切换到GPT-6 Astra来做我们的biomedical内部的任务了。我主要是做AI for Science，里面核心的就是AI for一些biomedical的应用。 我们用Astra有两个特别好用的地方，一个是Computer Use，一个是一些长程的任务。 Computer Use这方面，我们会用Astra来操作一些生物医学领域很多年前编写的那些软件，这些软件在领域内默认要使用，但它们其实都非常难用，界面设计的也不好，还有很多的术语，所以对一些跨领域的人来说，使用成本是非常高的。 但是Astra它的Computer Use功能，可以直接根据一些简单的prompt，就可以操作得比较好。并且我还可以跟它学习怎么用这个软件，毕竟在生物医学领域，很多人对AI工具的接受度比较低。 Astra可能把这些软件对应的在网上的一些教程，别人之前用过的一些用户日志，一些反馈全部都以文字的形式学进去了，所以它真的理解怎么用这些软件。 另一方面就是长程的任务，我们生物医学这块，任务会比较复杂，这些任务有时候会持续8至24小时，Astra会做得比较好。它比起其他的一些模型，做得比较慢，但挺让我放心的，说明它可能会更深思熟虑一点。 我们现在一般切换着用，白天用一些反馈比较快的模型，到了准备让模型跑一晚上的时候，就用Astra来设计一个比较长程的pipeline或者prompt。这也是它比较值得信赖的一点，在AI for Science这个领域里面的一些表现。 泓君：我没有想到Computer Use的这个功能居然在AI for Science领域能帮助到大家这么多。 王晟：Astra在这次发布时候做了两个生物医学的demo。其中一个就是Computer Use demo，这个demo在我们圈子内是出圈了，大家发现，原来可以直接用Astra来操作一个生物医学的tool。它当时操作的一个tool叫MultiQC，是一个挺常用的网页工具。我们开始用这个功能，发现它比想象的要好用很多。其实Computer Use这个功能我觉得之前的模型也具备，只是大家没有开始真的思考怎么把它融入我们科研中的pipeline里面。 computer use回春：但商业化卡在了身份验证 泓君：Bill，你可不可以一句话解释一下，什么是Computer Use？ 朱哲清：Computer Use是通过模型对于视觉的理解，来决定这个agent下一步要在屏幕上点击哪个部分，或者输入哪些文字，来完成一系列的任务。当它可以串联这么几十个动作的时候，可以完成一个最终人类想要达到的一个目的。 泓君：就它跟API的区别是，你不用给接口，不用给密码，它直接像人一样去操作跟使用电脑。 朱哲清：就是它看到的是人类看到的屏幕，看到人类看到的UI，看到人类看到的所有的视觉和可以交互的界面。通过人类可以使用的电脑的输入输出设备来完成这些任务。 Astra宣传片中展示的Computer Use场景 图片来源：OpenAI 泓君：我觉得Computer Use之前好像也有，为什么Astra的发布，又重新把Computer Use带火了？ 朱哲清：感觉Computer Use现在比原来又火了一波。之前大家觉得所有的工具都会开API，所有的工具都会有agent access（访问权限）的接口，很多的APP也好，系统也好，都在做agent native（原生智能体）的set up。 但是最近，不管是Instinct也好，还是Meta Muse也好，背后其实都接了浏览器。有一个比较大的问题就是有很多第三方的APP或者Amazon也好，比如说一些shopping的APP也好，travel的一些APP也好，他们其实是不愿意开放API的。 我觉得这又回到了当年Manus的情况，就是Manus最开始做了Browser 泓君：我看Claude最近有一个新的成果，就是他们发现了一种新酶系统ART，它有类似于CRISPR-Cas9的基因编辑的工具，但是它最后有没有被验证，还不太确定。在生物医药领域它已经开始有一些突破了，我们看到这些突破它的苗头是什么？ 王晟： 我们观察到这个突破几乎就正比于生物医学实验的周期，周期越短，反馈越快。 大家其实在过去的几十年中都积累了好多的实验数据，实验做得越快的领域，它模型就可以做得越好。譬如说Anthropic这次做的一个比赛，也是对酶的一个设计，这就是实验特别快的一个领域。未来像蛋白质酶这些可以做快速实验的，我觉得都会有很快的一个迭代。但如果譬如说我们要做一个衰老，或者研究一个罕见病，这种特定领域的长周期的问题，那我觉得模型的进展还是会很慢的。 泓君：酶跟蛋白质它带来的是哪些领域的变化？ 王晟：理论上蛋白质是万能的，减肥、癌症治疗、所有的病，理论上蛋白质都可以通过一些方式引导我们制药来治疗。酶是一种催化剂，更多是对各种工业化工的过程进行一些加工和加速，它的商业价值非常大，而且可以快速落地。那蛋白质呢，如果我还是要涉及药物，最后还是不可避免要做人体实验，还是有一个较长的周期。 普通人还有“蒸馏”的价值吗 ? 泓君：我也在跟很多模型的研究员去聊，很多前沿模型实验室的研究员就说，其实很多普通人他现在可能就连蒸馏的价值都没有了，这个话听上去很悲哀，是不是现在整个训练的信号也正在转向像专家数据和可验证环境，大家同意这个观点吗？ 许华哲：机器人领域这很显然不是这样的， 机器人领域每个人都是生活的专家 ，你擅长做饭，我擅长叠衣服，他擅长走路，他擅长跳舞。当然再往后走也会经历这样的一个阶段，也许一年两年后，必须要是一个舞蹈专家，或者必须要是一个Gordon Ramsay这样的大厨才值得被蒸馏。 王晟：如果知识被蒸馏的话，那确实现在AI的知识更全面，单个科学家肯定是比不过的。但是有一些科学发现，一些长期投入还是需要科学家或者工程师在那边支持背书，所以这方面是AI替代不了的。 同时也有一个反向蒸馏的问题，我天天也在蒸馏AI，尤其我们做AI for Science交叉学科的，很多东西我不知道，我就可以快速的向AI学习，学习之后我获取知识的速度也快，有时候有一些新的想法，新的创意，我可以做更好的一个科研成果，所以我觉得这是一个互相蒸馏的过程。 另一方面呢，如果从我们医学这个特定领域来说， 人的作用永远是非常大的，人不仅是解决问题，人还可以定义问题 。比如说有一些新的疾病，或者人想要活到200岁，活到500岁，这些问题都是源源不断的。然后每个人会有自己不同的身体状况，不停地提供给AI新的问题，所以普通人绝对不会被AI所取代。 朱哲清：从蒸馏的角度来说，因为我们现在的智力或者说模型的能力还是在非常大的模型，可能就是死记硬背了很多很多的知识在里面，以及一些know-how也是在训练当中硬加进去的。比如说你在优化一些benchmark呀，在推进固定的一些落地场景上面，你会做很多的overfitting（过拟合）的一个状态。在这种情况下，其实目前我们overfit的领域可能都还不够，有很多很多的领域值得被overfit。 我们现在都说，可能模型已经到了通用智能的这个级别，但是从我们目前在已经overfit的场景上面来说，可能没有到那么通用的状态。 后面如果我们要真的做到通用，可能还要跳出蒸馏每个场景，进入到模拟一个人从零开始学习的这么一个状态。 从这个角度来说，我们其实需要蒸馏的能力不在于说我能不能把这件事情做好，而是 蒸馏人是怎么学习，从零开始怎么比人学得还要快。 泓君：今天很难得啊，我们是把三个不同领域的，我觉得做得好的创业者跟学者请来了，大家要不要说一下，现在在你们领域里面，你自己最关心跟关注的一个问题？ 朱哲清：我们现在最关注的问题，其实就是目前硬件上面，全世界存储很有限，内存非常贵，显存非常贵，很多人又担心，是不是把所有的数据都上云了？如果说未来我们认为所有的计算和算力会被铺开，每个人都会有自己的算力，每一家公司也会有自己的算力。算力不再集中于只是在数据中心当中，我们是不是可以想象到，所有人都可以有自己的算力，可以运行自己的模型。这模型不一定说要做到最大，那我们能不能通过这些模型来解决生活当中百分之八九十的问题？解决现在AI不能够完全无限量普及的这么一个问题？ 我其实还是同意未来模型需要往更大、更强发展，比如说AI for Science上面，我可能需要一个非常高度很高的模型。而在正常的，比如说企业工作、个人生活当中，你可能需要一个广度很高的模型，这个模型不需要很大。那这个是一个结合的问题， 如果做好正确的结合，其实是可以解决目前的硬件需求和电力需求的瓶颈的。 许华哲：从机器人角度， 我们最关心的肯定还是零样本的泛化能力。 之前的机器人其实有两条路，一条是部署，一条是泛化，这两条路其实有一点正交。部署的话，有点像是AI赋能上一代的机器人，我在工厂里面的机械臂，原来可能是开环地拧螺丝，开环是指我不拿反馈。现在我有了AI，我可以闭环地拧螺丝，或者闭环地去上货。但是这件事情从我的视角来看，也还是有点逆时代的，你仍然需要5个博士水平的人在工厂里面睡3个月，去把这个机器人的稳定性啊、速度、是否要定制末端夹爪，这些事情全都解决。 但是今天我们聊Astra，我觉得最终我们还是希望是一个通用机器人。它零样本的可以做快速部署，这个部署应该是5个任意的、不用非常强的人放在那，这样的零样本泛化肯定是有冗余，这样的冗余我们是否可接受？我觉得是可接受的，在这种情况下，能否有一个足够好的、快的零样本泛化的模型，仍然是机器人最主要的追求。 泓君：你觉得机器人离那一步还有多远？ 许华哲：我觉得2028年初会是一个通用机器人比较开始真正实用的时间节点，从现在开始可能18个月后，大家可以在家里面以语言的形式去让一个机器人做家里面90%的事情。 泓君：这个预测是相当激进的。 许华哲：如果你玩了Astra，如果你下个月也许可以玩我们的模型，应该觉得这个预测还是比较合理的。 王晟： AI for Science，如果真的要有突破，最重要的就是AI对真实世界的理解，一个真实世界资源的运用、分配等等。 就像我们研究科学，本质就是研究真实世界——物理学研究宇宙，生物研究生命，化学研究微观世界。 但这个不是说我设计一个机器人去取代人类、自动地做实验，而是说AI知道：根据现在我实验室里有哪些资源，我应该让这个机器人、或者让这个人去做一些什么事。比如说以后我在prompt AI的时候，不是跟它说“给我设计一个药物能治疗癌症”，而是说“给你10万美金，你给我设计一个药物，并且我有这些实验可以做”，比如做一个老鼠实验要2000美金，做一个人体实验可能要一个怎么样的周期。 AI能够真的这样plan真实世界中超级复杂的任务，这些都是它的语料中很难见到的。这可能需要一个新的范式。就像现在我们都是人来用AI，人来研究怎么写好的prompt，可以把AI指挥好，怎么写好的prompt，怎么搭好的agent；未来可能是AI要写出清晰的、可执行的指令，是AI来prompt这个真实世界——非常高效，非常清晰，没有歧义。人或者机器人可以根据这些指令去利用现实世界中的资源，高效地把这些事情完成。 就像以前我们都说判断AI能不能遵循人的指令，未来我们可能要的是指令生成——它能不能生成更好的指令，帮助我们调动现实世界的资源。甚至我们还会对现实世界进行一些改造：未来的一些实验设备仪器，它不是给人看的，不是给人用的，是让AI用的。我们现在比如说拍X光、拍CT，还要合成一下图片，为了让人类医生能看；未来可能直接就拿出底层那些波形或者信号，直接给AI看就行了，都可以跳过生成图片那一步。 所以这是我认为最重要的，就是AI能够更好的走到真实世界中——无论是通过机器人，还是一个真实的人类——但它都要知道怎么样去利用真实世界的资源，来解决这种超难的问题。 本文来源： 硅谷101 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 美股高位，美国民众却愈发焦虑：消费者信心跌至五个月低点，通胀预期连续两月攀升
articles.summary: 美国消费者信心在持续通胀压力下进一步走弱，通胀预期同步升温，华尔街与普通民众之间的经济感受分化已扩大至历史极值。 密歇根大学10月消费者信心指数终值录得48，较9月的48.1小幅回落，触及五个月低点。尽管如此，该终值仍高于初值，并超出彭博调查中所有经济学家的预期。 消费者未来一年通胀预期从上月的4.6%升至4.7%，未来五至十年长期通胀预期亦从3.4%升至3.5%，两项指标均为今年5月以来最高，且均连续第二个月上行。 密歇根大学调查主任Joanne Hsu表示，"在通胀连续五年高于目标水平之后，短期和长期通胀预期近几个月均出现上行，这带来了通胀预期可能根深蒂固的风险。" 与此同时，标普500总回报指数已攀升至历史高位，而消费者信心却徘徊于历史低点附近，两者之间的背离创下罕见极值。 高物价侵蚀生活水准，跨党派担忧持续蔓延 调查显示，连续第四个月有越来越多的消费者主动提及高物价正在拖累其个人财务状况——10月这一比例升至56%，相比今年1月的45%显著上升。 这一趋势在各政治倾向群体中普遍存在，其中共和党选民的比例上升幅度最为突出。相比之下，最富裕消费者群体自1月以来对高价格负担的感受变化不大。 汽油价格是通胀担忧的重要来源之一——逾40%的受访者在未受任何引导的情况下主动提及油价问题，泵价持续保持在每加仑4美元以上。 Hsu指出，"所有政治倾向的消费者都一致认为，未来一年内通胀对经济构成的风险远大于失业。" 从政治立场来看，10月民主党和共和党选民的信心均出现小幅回升，但独立选民信心已连续第三个月下滑。消费者预期分项指数则自7月以来首次录得改善。 耐用品购买意愿跌至历史低位，利率压力凸显 当前状况分项指数跌至历史次低，其中耐用品购买条件指数单月骤降18%，为历史最低，主要原因是利率上升及购买力方面的顾虑加剧。 近70%的消费者预计未来一年利率还将继续上升，这一比例为逾三年来最高。 抵押贷款利率高企进一步拖累消费者购房及大额消费意愿。近几个月来，价格涨幅持续超越薪资增速，家庭预算压力持续积累。上周公布的数据亦显示，9月消费者价格涨幅创五个月新高。 华尔街与民众分化扩至历史极值 当前最引人注目的结构性背离或许并非来自数据本身，而是来自市场与民众之间的鲜明对比。标普500总回报指数已涨至历史高位，而密歇根大学消费者信心却接近历史低点——当前状况分项指数更跌至44.7的历史次低。 消费者信心较一年前下滑约10%，较今年2月高点下跌约15%。这一分化折射出两个截然不同的经济叙事： 股票市场受企业盈利增长、科技股集中效应及投资者乐观情绪驱动持续走强；而普通家庭则深陷高物价、高借贷成本与购买力萎缩的困境之中。历史上，此类股市与消费者信心之间的极端背离较为罕见。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 科技股大跌、美债走强，美股正在经历新一轮风格切换？
articles.summary: 美股市场正在出现明显分化：科技股遭遇重挫，标普500指数却有超过300只成分股收涨，美债则迎来2023年银行业危机以来最大单日收益率降幅。 周四的行情表明，科技股的抛售尚未演变为全市场普跌，资金对AI交易的态度也正在发生变化。 10月22日，标普500指数下跌1.2%，创7月以来最大单日跌幅；纳斯达克综合指数下跌2.6%，费城半导体指数重挫6.7%。与之形成鲜明对比的是，道指基本持平，小盘股指数罗素2000指数小幅收涨。标普500等权重指数也上涨0.7%，显示多数成分股的表现好于市值加权指数。 与此同时，10年期美债收益率下跌19.3个基点至4.952%，创2023年3月以来最大单日降幅。 科技股承压、债券走强、其他股票相对坚挺，令市场面临一个关键问题：这究竟是投资者从高估值AI资产撤出后的短期调整，还是美股持续数年的科技股主导行情正在发生变化？ 科技股与其他板块“分道扬镳” 据MarketWatch报道，周四超过300只标普500成分股收涨，但指数仍录得逾一个百分点的跌幅。 这种背离反映出美股内部日益明显的分化：少数高权重科技股的下跌，足以抵消大量其他股票的上涨。 AI交易此前推动美股持续走高，但随着相关企业公布业绩、披露资本开支计划，投资者开始更加关注巨额AI投入何时能够转化为实际回报。 周四，半导体板块跌幅尤其显著，费城半导体指数较6月高点已回落超过26%，进入技术意义上的熊市区间。 与科技股形成对比的是，消费必需品等防御性板块表现相对坚挺。市场策略师Mark Hackett指出，2026年以来，美股的板块领涨格局频繁变化，AI股票与其他板块之间的走势分化日益突出。 不过，个股上涨面较广，并不等于新一轮风格切换已经确立。若科技股持续走弱，而其他板块能够维持相对强势，资金才可能逐步从少数大型科技股向更广泛的市场扩散。 美债收益率大幅下行，避险需求升温 股市调整之际，美债迎来强劲买盘。周四，10年期美债收益率下跌19.3个基点至4.952%，创2023年3月银行业危机以来最大单日降幅。2年期美债收益率也大幅下行，反映出投资者对利率前景和短期风险的重新评估。 债券走强与科技股下跌同步发生，说明投资者正在调整资产配置、寻求更具防御性的投资选择。但这并不必然意味着市场已转向衰退交易。地缘政治紧张局势、油价上涨，以及对美联储后续利率路径的重新判断，也可能共同推动资金流向美债。 因此，周四行情更值得关注的并非单日涨跌，而是市场内部的资金偏好是否正在持续变化。如果科技股继续承压，其他板块维持强势，且美债需求保持旺盛，那么美股可能进入更广泛的风格再平衡阶段；反之，如果科技股止跌反弹，周四的分化也可能只是一次短期调整。 眼下，AI交易仍是观察美股走势的关键变量。市场并非简单地从看多转向看空，而是在重新衡量AI投资的回报、科技股的估值，以及其他行业的相对吸引力。新一轮风格切换是否真正形成，还需要更多交易日的表现来验证。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

选取了四组指标：VIX期限结构、VVIX、CBOE看跌/看涨期权比率以及SKEW指数。VIX和看跌/看涨期权比率等常规“一阶”指标仍显示市场平稳、风险偏好较强；而VVIX和SKEW等“二阶”指标已明显抬升，VVIX升至110~120，VIX期限结构近端也已倒挂。这说明个股层面的多头大多尚未对冲，但大型宏观机构已在指数层面大量买入深度虚值看跌期权，为尾部风险提前投保，风险层由此出现分层。 在此基础上，做市商在过去一年持续累积负德尔塔敞口，伽马也再度转负。负伽马状态下，做市商的对冲行为会从“高抛低吸”变为“越跌越卖”，市场的阻尼器作用正在快速减弱，与2015年A股股灾中杠杆资金被迫平仓、越跌越卖的机制相似。 核心结论：这些信号并不意味着市场马上会出问题，但一旦价格破位，下跌的自我强化机制可能被迅速启动，引发流动性真空或闪崩。风险的传导遵循从二阶到一阶的顺序，先体现在尾部对冲上，最后才反映到VIX和个股期权上，因此观察风险要分层看、提前看。 一、换一个维度：从市场层转向风险层 在前几期节目中，我们讲了“台风”和“阻尼器”，主要是从市场内部做分层、做“缩圈”，通过不同股票、不同板块之间的比较，观察“台风”对市场的影响以及市场内部的分化。今天我不再展开讲“台风”本身，因为它已经非常明确了：无论是能源、通胀还是利率，我相信大家都已经能感知到“台风”的变化。市场分层所用的数据和结构，前面也已经花了很多时间讲解；各国市场之间的差异，在过去两周也都已经走了出来。 今天我们换一个维度，从风险层来观察。前面讲的是市场层，这一次讲的是风险层， 从市场层再到风险层，我们才能看清 “ 台风 ” 在市场内部传导的完整路径。 这里我先放四组数据，都是日常应该使用和观察的指标。 第一组是VIX的期限结构。很多人其实已经注意到了这组数据。我放了标准的30天期VIX、近端的9天期VIX（VIX9D）以及远端的VIX（VIX3M），并分别计算了近端与标准VIX、标准VIX与远端之间的比值，以此观察波动率的期限结构。当然，也可以直接用VIX期货曲线来看。目前，VIX曲线的短端，大约一直到2026年年底的合约，已经开始呈现倒挂（backwardation），也就是超近端9天期的短期波动率已经超过了作为基准的30天期波动率。这就是当前VIX市场的结构。 第二组是VVIX，即VIX的波动率，也就是“波动率的波动率”，它衡量的是整个期权市场是否稳定。大家可以看到，目前VVIX已经超过110甚至120，这意味着整个市场里的对冲工具是紧张、稀缺的，大家都在疯狂寻找波动率的对冲工具。 这是典型的流动性开始趋紧的预警信号。 第三组是芝加哥期权交易所（CBOE）的看跌/看涨期权比率。这里面有几类，大家一定要注意区分：有指数期权的对冲，有个股期权的对冲，还有全市场的综合对冲。 第四组是SKEW指数，它衡量的是尾部风险。SKEW本质上反映的是深度虚值看跌期权相对于普通看跌期权的溢价，主要防范的是极端风险，也就是尾部风险。 以上这些指标，都是从波动率的角度去观察风险。我之前讲过，在美股市场上买期权，某种程度上就是在买保险，因此风险层主要就是通过这几个维度去观察。 二、风险分层：常规指标平静，二阶指标已发出尾部风险信号 从这几张图来看，我们大致可以把这些指标分成左右两侧。 从左侧的常规数据来看，无论是VIX，还是指数和个股的看跌/看涨期权比率，市场整体都还没有反映出大问题，看起来仍然是一片祥和，风险偏好依然很强。 但右侧的VVIX和SKEW指数都属于“二阶”指标，它们已经拉出了潜在尾部风险的信号。 从两类数据的差异可以看出，市场内部的风险层已经开始分层。 简单理解就是：从个股的看跌/看涨期权来看，目前个股层面还没有出现大的系统性利空，大家并没有在个股上做任何对冲；但那些掌握全局的大型机构，已经在底层的指数上建立风险防御，在大量买入深度虚值的看跌期权。所谓深度虚值看跌期权，举例来说，假设现在指数在5000点，他们大量买入的是4000点以下的看跌期权。 这类期权防范的并不是小幅波动。如果市场只是正常波动，这些期权基本没有用处。他们现在愿意花钱买这份“保险”，说明他们认为需要防范市场出现重大风险。这实际上就是我讲的“台风”向下传导的过程。此时应该先对冲哪一层？一定是先对冲小概率的风险，随着“台风”一层层刮过来，再逐步转向其他层面。 常规指标往往是最后才反应的，等到市场真正出现踩踏时，风险才会体现在这些常规指标上。 所以我们要分层去看、透过表象去看，先从二阶的维度去观察。 从当前的数据来看，可以理解为“台风”已经刮过来了，但市场表面看起来仍然很安静：从个股层面看，大部分多头实际上都没有进行对冲；但最近的数据显示，一些大型宏观交易机构已经开始在二阶层面进行对冲，这会进一步影响到处在中间位置的做市商。因此，我们还需要往下看一层，看看做市商的持仓情况。 三、负伽马与负德尔塔：市场的 “ 阻尼器 ” 正在减弱 接下来看做市商的持仓。这里有两个重要的指标，一个是德尔塔（Delta），一个是伽马（Gamma）。伽马主要看正负，德尔塔主要看累积的是正值还是负值。从数据上看，目前市场处于负伽马状态，同时做市商累积了大量的负德尔塔敞口。 大家应该都知道，做市商采取的是中性策略：你丢过来多单，我一定对冲出去；你丢过来空单，我也一定对冲出去。所以它追求的一定是德尔塔中性。德尔塔反映的是敞口和规模的问题，伽马反映的则是速度的问题。伽马为正时，做市商的对冲行为简单讲就是高抛低吸，可以机械式地把波动熨平，所以正伽马一般对应低波动。负伽马则是非常不好的状态：当所有机构都疯狂地向做市商寻求同一方向的头寸时，负伽马就会演变成恶性循环，对应的一般是高波动。说到底，负伽马就是“左脚踩右脚”：越是下跌，做市商越要对冲，越要对冲就越要卖出，越卖越跌，越跌越卖，最终可能导致闪崩。 当年的股灾其实也是这样。2015年A股股灾时，虽然我们的衍生品规模没有那么大，但市场基本上也出现了类似情况：杠杆资金以及承受赎回压力的公募基金等机构陷入了类似负伽马的状态，不得不持续平仓、减仓，形成越跌越亏、越亏越卖的循环。 再回到这张图。左边的德尔塔数据显示，最近一年里负德尔塔敞口在不断累积。这可以理解为，一些大机构和大资金在持续买入看跌期权进行对冲；而做市商作为交易对手，为保持中性，就会相应地卖出股票和股指，是一种机械性的做空，市场因此处于资金净流出的状态。这对市场构成了压制。当然，这种压制还要放到我们前面讨论的市场本身的结构里去看。而现在伽马再次转负，意味着做市商不得不顺着跌势在盘中加剧抛售。我估计这个负值在未来三个月很可能会进一步加大，需要密切留意。 也就是说，市场整体已经不再是正伽马状态下那种“你跌了有人接、你涨多了有人帮你缓冲”的格局，而可能转变为越跌越卖、越卖越跌。这就像我们之前举的深圳赛格大厦的例子： 负伽马意味着市场的阻尼器作用正在快速减弱，内部共振可能因此 “ 左脚踩右脚 ” ，使风险被放大。 把这些连在一起看：外部的“台风”风险已经在市场内部引发了风险的分化。在远端市场，我们已经看到机构在做尾部风险保护，一些机构的对冲已经比较拥挤，因此做市商累积了大量的负德尔塔敞口；同时，做市商自身的伽马已经转负。这告诉我们，风险正在一层层地分化，不同的人在为不同的风险层支付不同的溢价。 它并不是在告诉我们市场马上就要出问题，而是在告诉我们：一旦触发，下跌的自我循环机制可能会被迅速启动。 从当前市场来看，多头稍有反弹，就可能遇到做市商负德尔塔带来的抛压；而一旦稍有破位，那些聪明的宏观基金此前买入的远期虚值期权就会获得几倍甚至几十倍的收益，用来对冲其持有的正股风险。与此同时，破位之后，负伽马会迫使做市商加大抛售，简单讲就是越跌越砸。用我的话说，这种状态很容易引发市场流动性的突然真空，或者突然跳水。 最后，风险才会反映到最上面这一层，也就是左侧的VIX上；机构也才会逐渐从风险的二阶层面进入一阶层面，直接用个股期权进行对冲，风险由此直接反映到个股身上。这就是我所讲的风险分层的逻辑。 通过今天这些工具的分析，希望能帮助大家更好地理解：“台风”穿过市场之后，我们不仅可以通过市场结构的分层和缩圈观察它，还可以从风险层的结构和缩圈去理解它。今天就跟大家分享到这里，谢谢大家。 《付鹏说》第七季 articles.title: 补贴农民、松绑俄柴油、催欧洲放储备…特朗普“多管齐下”仍难压住柴油价
articles.summary: 距离11月3日美国中期选举不足两周，特朗普政府正以日益高昂的政治与财政代价，向一个顽固的问题发起多线进攻——柴油价格。 然而，一系列密集出台的措施—— 向农民撒出80亿美元补贴、允许红色染料柴油上路、松绑俄罗斯柴油制裁、向欧洲盟友施压释放应急储备——均未能扭转油价走势。 据美国能源信息署数据， 美国柴油均价上周再度上涨近10美分，至每加仑6.28美元，逼近历史高位，此前两周的短暂回落就此终结 。路透社/益普索10月民调显示，近八成美国人将高物价归咎于特朗普，令共和党在国会两院的微弱多数席位面临更大压力。 分析人士普遍对上述措施的实际效果持怀疑态度。宾夕法尼亚州穆伦堡学院民调专家、政治学者Chris Borick表示："总统倾向于以短期收益换取长期损失，而我怀疑这里是否真的存在任何短期收益。" 农业补贴创历史新高，但无法直接压低油价 特朗普本周一在堪萨斯州竞选集会上宣布，美国农业部将启动名为"丰收燃料救济计划"的新项目，向农民提供80亿美元资金，用于抵消本次收割季的柴油成本。农业部确认，这笔资金将以一次性支付形式发放，定位为应对"临时性市场扰动和生产成本上升"的短期救济，但明确指出仅覆盖"部分模型损失"，并非全额补偿。 这笔新增资金将使今年联邦对农民的总支付额推升至创纪录的554亿美元，超过2020年疫情期间创下的450亿美元历史峰值。 然而，补贴并不能直接作用于市场价格。全国农民联盟主席Rob Larew批评称："这是今年第二轮应急援助，用于弥补本可预见的损失。贸易中断和与海外冲突相关的燃料成本上涨，已令家庭农场陷入困境，而一次性支付无法为他们提供规划未来所需的稳定性。" 农业部目前尚无法说明资金将如何分配、何时到账，以及是否需要国会批准。 红色染料柴油令放，执行层面仍存模糊地带 特朗普本月签署行政令，允许卡车司机将通常用于农业机械等非公路用途的红色染料柴油用于公路行驶，并暂时豁免部分联邦税务申报和记录要求。 但美国国税局并未取消联邦柴油税，仅暂时豁免相关申报要求及罚款至年底，令加油站和燃料销售商面临不确定性。代表美国最大卡车停靠站运营商的行业协会NATSO首席游说人David Fialkov表示，成员对特朗普应对柴油成本的努力表示赞赏，但相关指引仍"模糊不清"，风险过高。"我实在看不出这些染料柴油公告能对柴油价格产生任何实质性影响，"他说。 俄罗斯柴油重返美国，地缘代价引发两党批评 在增加供应端，特朗普政府选择松绑对俄罗斯柴油的制裁。 据路透社报道，LSEG航运数据显示， 马耳他籍油轮Agioi Fanendes已于10月22日在俄罗斯波罗的海港口普里莫尔斯克装载4万吨超低硫柴油，目的地为美国，预计11月7日抵达纽约。 俄罗斯总统新闻秘书佩斯科夫当日确认，根据俄美达成的协议，俄对美柴油供应已正式启动。 特朗普此前宣布， 俄罗斯将立即出口30万吨柴油，11月增至50万吨，此后进一步扩大至100万吨。 俄罗斯副总理诺瓦克上周表示，俄方有望在年底前将柴油月出口量恢复至300万至350万吨的常规水平。 然而，这一举措在国内引发两党批评。原本旨在限制莫斯科能源收入、削弱其资助乌克兰战争能力的制裁被松绑，其地缘政治代价显而易见。分析人士指出，伊朗冲突才是本轮柴油价格飙升的主要驱动因素，乌克兰对俄罗斯炼油厂的打击虽有一定影响，但作用相对有限。对外关系委员会Maurice R. Greenberg中心主任Edward Fishman表示："我更多地将其视为一种转移责任的替罪羊操作，而非在选举前真正试图平抑价格的举措。" 白宫将高价归咎于"历史遗留问题"，政治压力持续升温 白宫将高柴油价格归因于"既有问题"，包括多年来的炼油厂关闭以及俄乌战争造成的破坏，同时为特朗普的系列举措进行辩护。白宫发言人Taylor Rogers表示："总统希望柴油价格下降，这正是他采取历史性行动、为美国农民、卡车司机和工人守住每一分血汗钱的原因。" 政治压力在传统共和党农业州尤为突出。爱荷华州、堪萨斯州等地的农民面临燃料和化肥成本上涨、贸易中断及农业经济疲软的多重压力，部分特朗普核心支持者的不满情绪正在积聚。特朗普已在该地区的竞选集会上大力宣传上述柴油措施，并在内布拉斯加州当众签署行政令。 分析人士普遍认为，在中期选举前，上述措施难以带来实质性的价格缓解。随着选举日临近，特朗普政府正在为一场效果存疑的价格保卫战付出越来越高的代价。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 法国PMI全线跌破荣枯线，欧元区10月综合PMI初值降至51.9逊于预期
articles.summary: 法国经济意外陷入收缩，令欧元区10月商业活动增速超预期放缓，市场对欧元区财政稳定与增长韧性的担忧同步升温。 法国10月综合PMI初值骤降至48.4，跌破50荣枯线，远低于彭博调查预期的50.3，9月终值为51.1。服务业与制造业双双萎缩，构成全面压力。欧元区整体10月综合PMI初值随之降至51.9，低于彭博预期的52.7，9月为53.1。德国综合PMI虽连续第四个月位于扩张区间，报52.8，但同样低于预期。 法国基准国债收益率本周触及5%，为2002年以来首次，法德利差扩大至约175个基点，创2011年以来最阔。Franklin Templeton固定收益投资主管警告，若法债抛售升级为欧元区债务危机，其烈度可能超过十多年前那场危机。 法国：综合、服务业、制造业均低于50 法国10月综合PMI初值为48.4，9月为51.1。服务业PMI为48.4，制造业PMI为49.3，两个分项和综合指数均低于50。彭博称，法国财政担忧引发国债抛售，国内还出现抗议与骚乱。 S&P Global Market Intelligence经济学家Joe Hayes表示，9月反弹被证明短暂，金融条件迅速收紧、政治压力进一步上升并不令人意外。私营部门销售量以5月以来最快速度下降，并立即体现为采购与投资活动减少。 Hayes称，10月数字可能只是前奏。企业对未来12个月预期的情绪指标已降至六年半低点，反映出对2027年总统选举高度不确定性及财政状况的担忧。 德国：连续第四个月扩张，增速放缓 德国10月综合PMI初值为52.8，9月为53.8，路透调查预期53.3，彭博调查预期53.4。该指数已连续第四个月位于扩张区间，但低于预期。 制造业： PMI升至54.2的两月高点，9月为53.9，工厂产出继续强劲上升。不过制造业订单增速降至三个月低点，仍受出口支撑。 服务业： PMI为51.7，前值52.9，连续第二个月扩张但幅度温和。服务业需求停滞，原因是客户推迟决策、收紧预算。 整体： 私营部门新业务仅略增。商品与服务收费价格通胀降至七个月低点，但仍明显高于长期均值。 S&P Global Market Intelligence经济学家Phil Smith表示，结果令人鼓舞地显示德国商业活动持续回升，但增长放缓突显出欧元区最大经济体的复苏仍然脆弱。 企业对未来12个月产出总体仍乐观，服务业信心升至2月以来最高，制造商预期则降至7月以来最低，原因是担忧投入价格上升。 欧元区：法国服务业拖累增长 欧元区10月综合PMI初值为51.9，9月为53.1，仍明显高于50。彭博称，私营部门放缓程度超出预期，法国表现逊于预期，德国制造业则强于预期。 S&P Global Market Intelligence首席商业经济学家Chris Williamson表示，增长的主要拖累是法国服务业活动再度下降，这或与罢工和骚乱扰乱部分地方经济有关。他同时指出，整个地区10月的活动“是过去三年部分最佳表现之一”。 据彭博报道，欧元区经济对伊朗战争及随之而来的能源价格冲击表现出韧性。但也有人担心，中东冲突持续和债市收益率急升将拖累经济活动。 债市压力与ECB路径 彭博称，法国基准国债收益率本周触及5%，为2002年以来首次。法德利差扩大至近175个基点，为2011年以来最阔。能源价格上涨加剧了市场对法国财政前景的担忧，法国同时面临沉重的预算赤字和疲软的增长。 Franklin Templeton固定收益投资主管周三警告，法债抛售若升级为又一次欧元区债务危机，可能比十多年前那次更糟。 在政策层面，欧洲央行（ECB）因通胀高于目标已加息两次，并示意可能仍需进一步收紧。官员们被广泛预期下周维持借贷成本不变。 高级欧元区经济学家David Powell表示，综合PMI显示经济开始在更高的商品价格与更紧的金融条件下走弱。他认为这几乎肯定会让ECB在10月按兵不动，并在12月最后一次加息后结束加息周期。 Williamson则指出，投入成本再度急剧上升，企业为保护利润推高售价。“持续增长与顽固偏高通胀”的组合，或加剧市场对ECB更激进收紧的猜测。他表示，更高的借贷成本已开始通过抑制需求显现影响。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
